name: Active Play & Outdoors
blurb: Activity guidelines, sedentary time, outdoors, swimming and massage

claims.claim: Infant massage supports growth and development
claims.testedAs: Infant massage supports growth and development

aap.says: Baby massage supports your baby's physical wellness and their emotional and psychological development.

claims.query: infant massage therapy growth weight gain development preterm

claims.claim: More outdoor time in early childhood reduces the risk of myopia
claims.testedAs: More outdoor time in early childhood reduces the risk of myopia

nhs.says: Spending more time outdoors, especially for children, can help stop short-sightedness getting worse. NHS frames this as slowing progression, not preventing onset.

aap.says: Balancing screen time with time outside may help limit your child's short-sightedness and protect their vision as they grow.

claims.query: outdoor time children myopia incidence prevention light exposure

claims.claim: Infant swimming programmes improve motor skill development
claims.testedAs: Infant swimming programmes improve motor skill development
claims.query: infant swimming aquatic programme motor skill development outcomes

claims.claim: Infants should have at least 30 minutes of tummy time or active play daily
claims.testedAs: Greater daily tummy time or active play in infancy is associated with better motor development

nhs.says: Babies under 1 should get at least 30 minutes of tummy time a day, spread across the day while awake.

aap.says: Start with 2 to 3 short sessions a day from birth and build up to 15 to 30 minutes a day by about 7 weeks, more as babies grow.

guidance.note: The NHS sets a floor of at least 30 minutes of tummy time a day across the first year, while the AAP frames it as gradually building up to 15 to 30 minutes a day by around 7 weeks, with more as the baby gets stronger.

claims.query: infant physical activity guideline 30 minutes tummy time daily recommendation

claims.claim: Prolonged sedentary or restrained time is associated with poorer development
claims.testedAs: Prolonged sedentary or restrained time is associated with poorer development

nhs.says: Long stretches of sitting still or being strapped into a buggy or car seat are not good for an under-5's health and development.

aap.says: Babies who spend too long in car seats, swings, bouncy seats or strollers may be slower to reach motor milestones.

claims.query: sedentary behaviour restraint infant toddler developmental outcomes
